beats.label: Give it a key but not consent
beats.cue: The kill switch. The adapter refuses to even construct until you opt in to owning this Mac's logged-in iMessage account — exit 1, no socket, no chat.db.
beats.script: The kill switch. The adapter refuses to even construct until you opt in to owning this Mac's logged-in iMessage account — exit 1, no socket, no chat.db. [[pause:1.5s]] The refusal is the proof in this beat, so the verifier expects exit code 1. Designed refusal `IMessageAdapterError: iMessage adapter requires CREWHAUS_IMESSAGE_HOST_ENABLED=1 (opt-in to host's logged-in iMessage)`. The dummy key only clears the env-name gate above; nothing reaches a provider.

verify.note: designed refusal — `IMessageAdapterError: iMessage adapter requires CREWHAUS_IMESSAGE_HOST_ENABLED=1 (opt-in to host's logged-in iMessage)`. The dummy key only clears the env-name gate above; nothing reaches a provider. Off macOS the same beat exits 1 on the platform check instead. Note the throw is at daemon.ts module scope, outside main().catch(), so it prints a raw Bun trace rather than a formatted failure report.

beats.label: Boot the daemon for real
beats.cue: [needs-key] Opting in is a whole extra env var, on purpose. It serves the gateway on PORT — 3000 by default. Backgrounded, so this same terminal can keep going.
beats.script: Opting in is a whole extra env var, on purpose. It serves the gateway on PORT — 3000 by default. Backgrounded, so this same terminal can keep going. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay. Needs Anthropic credentials plus the host opt-in; prints the janitor report then `[daemon] listening on http://localhost:3000` and stays up.

verify.note: needs Anthropic credentials plus the host opt-in; prints the janitor report then `[daemon] listening on http://localhost:3000` and stays up. Full Disk Access (chat.db) and Automation (AppleScript send) are only asked for by an actual poll/send — the daemon's boot path touches neither, so macOS does not prompt here. Deps were installed by the --check beat. Re-take housekeeping: `kill %1` (or a fresh terminal) before a second take, or :3000 is still held.

beats.label: Ask why no conversation appeared
beats.cue: Because nothing polled. The daemon registers the adapter and serves the gateway; draining chat.db is a call you own, on whatever cadence you want.
beats.script: Because nothing polled. The daemon registers the adapter and serves the gateway; draining chat.db is a call you own, on whatever cadence you want. [[pause:1.5s]] Four lines from the adapter make that ownership explicit: the host must call pollNewMessages. The generated daemon does not run a poll loop, so the caller chooses the schedule; no background polling is implied.

verify.note: 4 matching lines, in the adapter's own words: "the adapter exposes `pollNewMessages()` for the host to call; the generated channel daemon does NOT run a poll loop, so the caller is responsible for driving polling on whatever schedule it likes." Verified against the emitted bundle: `grep -n poll live/dist/daemon.ts` matches nothing, so .crewhaus/sessions stays empty no matter who texts this Mac — the earlier `ls .crewhaus/sessions` beat promised a payoff the bundle cannot deliver and was replaced by this one.
